item.title: 11 mil reproducciones · 658 reacciones | O ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), determinou que o diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, entregue até as 23h deste domingo (13) uma cópia integral dos dados extraídos do celular de Daniel Vorcaro, apreendido na Operação Compliance Zero. A decisão intensifica a disputa entre ministros sobre o acesso ao material. André Mendonça se opõe à divulgação, alegando risco à investigação. A PF informou ao presidente do STF, Edson Fachin, que pode fornecer cópias a qualquer ministro. Gilmar Mendes, Zanin e Alexandre de Moraes pressionam pelo acesso antes da sessão de terça-feira, que analisará conversas atribuídas a Vorcaro e Moraes. A PGR também pediu acesso aos dados. ➡️ Assista ao #JornalGloboNews na TV e no @globoplay #GloboNews | GloboNews

item.title: Andy Burnham to host entrepreneurs and local mayors at No 10 on Monday
item.description: Prime minister vows to ‘reindustrialise Britain’ through new partnership with business The prime minister is to host business leaders, entrepreneurs and local mayors at Downing Street on Monday to pitch his government as a “partner for growth” that can offer a stable platform for investment and jobs in the UK. Ahead of the event, Andy Burnham said the country had “everything it needs to succeed”, including talented people and world-class universities, but requires “a culture shift in how Britain does business” if it is to unlock its full potential. item.title: Trump to consider releasing 9/11 records after families’ request
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he will look into requests from families of September 11 victims to release records that could shed light on Saudi Arabia’s alleged role in the attacks 25 years ago. Several families have long alleged that a group of extremist religious leaders in Saudi Arabia gained influence in the Saudi government and aided the hijackers. Fifteen of the 19 hijackers were Saudis but the Saudi government has long denied any involvement in the attacks. The families have... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Donald Trump ahora quiere ver "una Irlanda unificada", pero con un solo objetivo: desintegrar el Reino Unido y desestabilizar a Europa
item.description: Este domingo el presidente norteamericano volvió a mencionar la más conflictiva resultante del acuerdo del Viernes Santo, que puso fin a la guerra civil religiosa entre civiles y protestantes en Irlanda del Norte, con la mediación —entre otros— de Estados Unidos: la posibilidad de una Irlanda unida. El objetivo del magnate no es "naive" ni una torpeza, sino que busca dañar la integridad del reino, su ex aliado transatlántico, como lo hizo con Canadá o con Malvinas. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.

item.description: Si los partidos de izquierda se alinean con la OTAN, restringen la inmigración y asumen como prioridad la seguridad en los barrios tomados por las bandas criminales de origen extranjero, entonces los votantes de Suecia les devuelven el voto. Eso es lo que se desprende este domingo de los resultados de las elecciones suecas, en un recuento muy ajustado. Unions accuse Sapin of promoting far-right ideas ahead of next spring's presidential election, while management has defended the appointment in the name of pluralism. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Canada explores ‘associate member’ status with EU amid US trade tensions
item.description: Canada explores becoming an associate member of the European Union. Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks stronger economic and strategic ties with the bloc. This move comes as Canada's trade relationship with the United States has worsened. Discussions focus on free movement of goods, services, and workers. Deeper cooperation is also being considered in energy and technology sectors. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Pressure builds in Spain to deny US extradition request for leftwing donor
item.description: Key government meeting this month will consider US bid to try James ‘Fergie’ Chambers over alleged support for Hamas Attorneys for James “Fergie” Chambers, the US citizen and wealthy donor to leftwing and humanitarian projects worldwide who is currently imprisoned in Madrid and sought in extradition, have submitted a brief ahead of a decisive government meeting on the case. Meanwhile, Chambers’ partner, the actor and activist Stella Schnabel, met last week with multiple members of the Spanish parliament to assert his innocence. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Only slim chance target of building 1.5m homes in England will be met, minister says
item.description: Angela Rayner says manifesto pledge is not being dropped but focus is now on building council houses UK politics live – latest updates The government is unlikely to meet its target of building 1.5m homes in England, Angela Rayner has acknowledged, saying there was only a “slim chance” enough houses would be built before the next election. The manifesto pledge to build 1.5m houses by the next election was a “stretch target”, the communities secretary added, but said it was not being ditched and she was “definitely not giving up”. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Voting under way in Sweden with far right eyeing first role in government
item.description: Race too close to call and may take days to become clear despite early exit polls suggesting left bloc win Sweden general election – live updates With most of the votes counted, Sweden’s national election remained too close to call on Sunday night, with left-wing parties holding a lead of just a single seat according to a partial tally by the election authority. Earlier in the night, exit polls suggested that the country was on course for a brand new left-leaning government. But as the votes were counted, it was apparent it could take days for the outcome to become clear. Continue reading... Publicado también por: Al Jazeera English. Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Swedes vote in election that could usher far right into government
item.description: Swedes are heading to the polls Sunday for a general election that will either bring a far right party into government for the first time or shift the country back towards the liberalism it has long been known for. The centre-left opposition holds a narrow lead over the ruling right-wing bloc but Prime ⁠Minister Ulf Kristersson's four-party alliance – which includes the far right Sweden Democrats – has been catching up in the final weeks of campaigning. item.title: Brazil: Michelle Bolsonaro's key role in the presidential race
item.description: Brazil is heading to the polls on October 4, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva seeking a fourth term as the Bolsonaro family mounts a political comeback through Flávio's presidential bid and Michelle's Senate campaign. With polls pointing to another tight race, Michelle's popularity among women could prove crucial as the family tries to return to power. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: George Osborne calls for UK to rejoin EU customs union and boost trade
item.description: Ex-Tory chancellor says economy has ‘fallen off a cliff’ since Brexit but rejoining union could be ‘quite simple’ The former chancellor George Osborne said Britain’s economy had “fallen off a cliff” since Brexit and that rejoining the European Union’s customs union would be the fastest route to recovery. Osborne, who was sacked as chancellor by Theresa May after being part of David Cameron’s cabinet at the time of the referendum, said it was important to rebuild links with the EU. Continue reading... item.title: Sweden election: A turning point for the far right?
item.description: The stakes are high in Sweden's general election, with the far right poised to enter government for the first time. TV4 News journalist Markus Karlsson-Bourrioux explains how opinion polls shifted from a comfortable centre-left lead to a tight race over the summer, and how far-right ideas have gained ground since the last election in 2022. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Germany: Thousands rally against far-right after AfD victory
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched in around 20 cities across Germany to protest the rise of the far right after the AfD's historic victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Demonstrators said they were defending democracy as mainstream parties continue to rule out governing with the AfD. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: ‘This is our home’: German minorities defy far-right AfD’s culture of fear after election win
item.description: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt has sent shockwaves through Germany and Europe as far-right parties continue to rise across the continent. Intense hostility has left migrants and minorities in fear of attacks and abuse, Alex Croft reports Fuente: The Independent - World.

item.title: Macron, Carney to visit North Atlantic French islands after Trump's map post
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will reaffirm the “sovereignty of nations” on a visit on September 20 to Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, a French territory in the North Atlantic, the Élysée Palace announced on Sunday. The symbolic trip comes after US President Donald Trump posted a map on social media showing the entire North American continent covered by the US flag. Fuente: France 24 - English.
